endorsements.quote: To close this gap, the European Commission could clarify that software processing clinical-grade health data and producing personalized health guidance is presumed to have a medical purpose under the MDR, unless explicitly demonstrated this is not the case.

unlisted_practices: Add health-focused generative AI systems to Annex XVI of the MDR or, by delegated act, to Annex III of the AI Act so they fall under the high-risk regime.
Require sector-specific safety regimes to evaluate medical AI systems for equity effects.

Develop harmonized GPSR standards for health-focused generative AI chatbots that require demonstrable performance against clinically relevant quality benchmarks and focus on functional role rather than declared intended purpose.

Clarify in consumer law, including the Digital Fairness Act, that presenting personalized health outputs so as to create a reasonable impression of clinical reliability without adequate validation is a misleading practice.

Clarify that large-scale aggregation of health data within generative AI advice systems triggers safeguards beyond GDPR compliance, with stricter limits on secondary commercial use such as AI training, profiling, targeted advertising, and third-party partnerships, and reinforced data minimization.

Establish that health data collected by AI chatbots for health advice cannot be repurposed for AI training unless users receive a separate, explicit, granular choice, independent of access to other services or incentives.
Establish closer cooperation between data protection authorities and health authorities for oversight of health-focused AI chatbots.
Consider benefit-sharing mechanisms, such as targeted taxation or data value return schemes, so that value derived from health data flows back to public health systems.

Subject AI systems operating as personalized health advisors at scale to proportionate duties of safety validation, transparency, equity monitoring, and accountability, irrespective of disclaimers or product labels.
Coordinate European and national regulators, including medical device, data protection, and consumer protection authorities, in overseeing health-focused generative AI chatbots.

screen.reason: This is a policy brief/commentary discussing the governance and regulatory gaps around health-focused generative AI chatbots from a European perspective.
